lede: The biggest item this week is Mountain Village Town Council taking up first reading of an ordinance that would move Housing Authority fees out of the municipal code and into an annually updated fee schedule — a structural shift in how affordable housing costs get set that's worth understanding before it advances. Meanwhile, the County's Housing Code SSR working group holds its eighth session Tuesday on Proposition 123-funded Land Use Code changes, the BOCC takes up a view-plain MOU tied to a 1999 settlement, and HARC weighs in on a potential demolition and new construction at Rebekah Hall — the building where they meet.

notable.stake: Policy vote on how 'subpar bedrooms' in mitigation units get handled going forward.
Working session shapes county Land Use Code changes affecting workforce housing production.
HARC considers demolition and new construction of Town-owned Rebekah Hall at 113 W Columbia.
BOCC acts on view-plain MOU and discusses two state constitutional amendments.
Two public hearings — Curry PUD and a parcel subdivision — open for public comment.
First reading: ordinance shifting MVHA fees out of municipal code into adjustable fee schedule.
